question.text: How far before a turn or lane change should you signal?

answer.text: Turn on your turn signal at least fifty feet before a turn or lane change.

teaching.text: the signal fifty feet ahead rule sets signaling at least fifty feet before a turn, while the turning just past an intersection rule says to wait until you are in the intersection when turning just past it. Remember: Fifty feet ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Turn on your turn signal at least fifty feet before a turn or lane change.

question.text: When should you signal if you plan to turn just past an intersection?

answer.text: If you plan to turn just past an intersection, wait until you are in the intersection to signal, so no one thinks you are turning at it.

teaching.text: the signal fifty feet ahead rule sets signaling at least fifty feet before a turn, while the turning just past an intersection rule says to wait until you are in the intersection when turning just past it. Remember: Signal once inside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you plan to turn just past an intersection, wait until you are in the intersection to signal, so no one thinks you are turning at it.

question.text: What should you not use your turn signal for?

answer.text: Do not use your turn signal to wave a driver behind you around, or to repeat the signals of cars ahead of you.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Changing lanes", but signals are required for lane changes. Remember: Signals are not waves.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not use your turn signal to wave a driver behind you around, or to repeat the signals of cars ahead of you.

question.text: Why should you signal even when no one seems to be around?

answer.text: Signal every time you change direction, even when no one seems to be around, because the car you do not see is the most dangerous.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "It is optional when alone", but signal every time. Remember: The unseen car matters.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Signal every time you change direction, even when no one seems to be around, because the car you do not see is the most dangerous.

question.text: How long should you signal when leaving a curb?

answer.text: When leaving a curb, signal long enough for oncoming traffic to know you are pulling out of the parked position.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "For one blink", but long enough for others to know. Remember: Signal long enough.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When leaving a curb, signal long enough for oncoming traffic to know you are pulling out of the parked position.

question.text: When should you move into the turn lane and choose your gear?

answer.text: Move into the correct turn lane as early as possible, sooner on faster roads, choose your gear before the intersection and accelerate slightly through the turn.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "At the last moment", but as early as possible. Remember: Early lane, early gear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Move into the correct turn lane as early as possible, sooner on faster roads, choose your gear before the intersection and accelerate slightly through the turn.

question.text: When should you not enter an intersection to turn?

answer.text: Do not enter an intersection to turn if traffic ahead could keep you from finishing the turn before the light changes; wait behind the stop line.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Enter anyway", but wait behind the stop line. Remember: Wait behind the line.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not enter an intersection to turn if traffic ahead could keep you from finishing the turn before the light changes; wait behind the stop line.

question.text: What should you do if you are in the wrong lane for a turn?

answer.text: If you are in the wrong lane for a turn, go on to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane there.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Cut across lanes to turn", but continue to the next intersection. Remember: Next intersection, right lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you are in the wrong lane for a turn, go on to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane there.

question.text: Why keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left?

answer.text: While waiting to turn left, keep your wheels pointed straight, because a rear-end hit with the wheels turned can push you into oncoming traffic.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "It saves tire wear", but the reason is avoiding being pushed into oncoming traffic. Remember: Straight wheels while waiting.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: While waiting to turn left, keep your wheels pointed straight, because a rear-end hit with the wheels turned can push you into oncoming traffic.

question.text: What should you not do during the turn itself?

answer.text: Do not brake or press the clutch during the turn itself, and do not shift gears in the intersection.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Look ahead", but looking ahead is fine. Remember: No braking mid-turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not brake or press the clutch during the turn itself, and do not shift gears in the intersection.

question.text: How do two drivers turning left from opposite directions pass each other?

answer.text: When two drivers meet at an intersection and both turn left, each turns to the left of the other.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Each turns to the right of the other", but each turns to the left of the other. Remember: Left of each other.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When two drivers meet at an intersection and both turn left, each turns to the left of the other.

question.text: When should you start turning the wheel in a left turn?

answer.text: In a left turn, keep the wheels straight until you reach the turn point, just before the imaginary center of the intersection.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "As soon as you enter the intersection", but wait until the turn point. Remember: Straight to the turn point.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a left turn, keep the wheels straight until you reach the turn point, just before the imaginary center of the intersection.

question.text: How do you make a left turn from a two-way street?

answer.text: For a left turn from a two-way street, approach in the lane next to the center line, then turn into the first lane just right of the center line of the new street, never wide into the right lane.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "The far right lane", but do not turn wide into the right lane. Remember: Center lane to center lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a left turn from a two-way street, approach in the lane next to the center line, then turn into the first lane just right of the center line of the new street, never wide into the right lane.

question.text: What should you do if the light turns yellow while you wait to turn left?

answer.text: If the light turns yellow while you are waiting to turn left, do not pull into the intersection.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Pull in quickly", but do not pull into the intersection. Remember: Yellow: do not pull in.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If the light turns yellow while you are waiting to turn left, do not pull into the intersection.

question.text: What color are center lines on two-way and one-way streets?

answer.text: Center lines are yellow on two-way streets and white on one-way streets.

teaching.text: the center line colors rule gives center line colors by street type, while the two-lane versus four-lane markings rule contrasts two-lane and four-lane highway center markings. Remember: Yellow two-way, white one-way.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Center lines are yellow on two-way streets and white on one-way streets.

question.text: Which lane do you enter when turning left onto a one-way street?

answer.text: Turning left onto a one-way street, turn sharply into the first lane, the one nearest the left curb.

teaching.text: the left turn from a one-way street rule sets the lane to turn left from on a one-way street, while the left turn onto a one-way street rule sets the lane to turn into on a one-way street. Remember: Nearest the left curb.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Turning left onto a one-way street, turn sharply into the first lane, the one nearest the left curb.

question.text: Which lane should you approach a left turn from on a one-way street?

answer.text: On a one-way street, approach a left turn from the lane farthest to the left.

teaching.text: the left turn from a one-way street rule sets the lane to turn left from on a one-way street, while the left turn onto a one-way street rule sets the lane to turn into on a one-way street. Remember: Farthest left lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a one-way street, approach a left turn from the lane farthest to the left.

question.text: Which lane must you use where a lane is marked for left turns?

answer.text: Where a lane is marked for left turns, turn only from that lane, and in multiple turn lanes stay in your starting lane all the way through.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Switch lanes mid-turn", but stay in your starting lane. Remember: Stay in your turn lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Where a lane is marked for left turns, turn only from that lane, and in multiple turn lanes stay in your starting lane all the way through.

question.text: Which lane do you enter turning left from a one-way onto a two-way street?

answer.text: Turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street, enter the intersection before turning sharply into the first lane right of the yellow line, and move right only after signaling and checking.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "The far right lane", but the first lane right of the yellow line. Remember: First lane right of yellow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street, enter the intersection before turning sharply into the first lane right of the yellow line, and move right only after signaling and checking.

question.text: May you turn left on red from a one-way street onto a two-way street?

answer.text: Turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street is never allowed on a red light.

teaching.text: the one-way onto one-way on red rule allows a left on red from one-way onto one-way, while the one-way onto two-way never on red rule forbids a left on red from one-way onto two-way. Remember: Never on red.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street is never allowed on a red light.

question.text: When may you turn left on red from one one-way street onto another?

answer.text: Turning left from one one-way street onto another, you may go on red after a full stop unless a No Turn on Red sign is posted.

teaching.text: the turns on red rule allows right on red and left on red from one-way onto one-way, and the one-way onto one-way on red rule details the one-way to one-way left turn on red. Remember: One-way to one-way on red.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Turning left from one one-way street onto another, you may go on red after a full stop unless a No Turn on Red sign is posted.

question.text: Which turns on red does Tennessee allow?

answer.text: Tennessee allows a right turn on red, and a left turn on red from a one-way street onto a one-way street going left, unless a sign forbids it, after a full stop and yielding.

teaching.text: the turns on red rule allows right on red and left on red from one-way onto one-way, and the one-way onto one-way on red rule details the one-way to one-way left turn on red. Remember: Right on red, signs permitting.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Tennessee allows a right turn on red, and a left turn on red from a one-way street onto a one-way street going left, unless a sign forbids it, after a full stop and yielding.

question.text: When may the second lane of a multiple turn lane make the same turn?

answer.text: In a multiple turn lane setup, the second lane may make the same turn as the first only when a sign or pavement marking allows it.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Always", but only when a sign or marking allows it. Remember: Only if marked.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a multiple turn lane setup, the second lane may make the same turn as the first only when a sign or pavement marking allows it.

question.text: What do white channel lines in an intersection do?

answer.text: White channel lines and arrows in an intersection guide you into the correct lane as you turn.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Mark parking spots", but they guide you into the correct lane. Remember: Channel lines guide you.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: White channel lines and arrows in an intersection guide you into the correct lane as you turn.

question.text: How should you make a right turn?

answer.text: On a right turn, do not swing wide to the left; stay close to the right curb and turn into the lane nearest the right curb.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Swing wide to the left first", but do not swing wide. Remember: Hug the right curb.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a right turn, do not swing wide to the left; stay close to the right curb and turn into the lane nearest the right curb.

question.text: What can happen if you swing wide before a right turn?

answer.text: If you swing wide before a right turn, the driver behind may think you are turning left and try to pass you on the right.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Nothing", but the driver behind may pass on the right. Remember: Wide swing invites passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you swing wide before a right turn, the driver behind may think you are turning left and try to pass you on the right.

question.text: What should you check before a right turn?

answer.text: Before a right turn, look left and right for cross traffic and for oncoming vehicles also turning, and check for pedestrians and bicyclists.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Only the light", but look for traffic, turners, pedestrians and bicyclists. Remember: Look both ways first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before a right turn, look left and right for cross traffic and for oncoming vehicles also turning, and check for pedestrians and bicyclists.

question.text: Why should you never pass a truck on the right if it may turn right?

answer.text: Large trucks and buses must swing wide when turning, so never pass one on the right if it may be turning right.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Trucks have no right mirror", but the reason is that trucks swing wide. Remember: Trucks swing wide.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Large trucks and buses must swing wide when turning, so never pass one on the right if it may be turning right.

question.text: Which way do you travel in a roundabout, and whom do you yield to?

answer.text: Always travel counterclockwise, to the right, around a roundabout, and yield to vehicles already circulating before entering.

teaching.text: the roundabout direction and yielding rule sets the direction and yielding in a roundabout, while the roundabout speed and exits rule sets speeds, passing and signaling to exit. Remember: Counterclockwise, yield inside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Always travel counterclockwise, to the right, around a roundabout, and yield to vehicles already circulating before entering.

question.text: What speeds, passing and exit rules apply in a roundabout?

answer.text: Roundabout speeds are usually posted at fifteen to twenty-five miles per hour, you may not pass inside a multi-lane roundabout, and you signal right to exit.

teaching.text: the roundabout direction and yielding rule sets the direction and yielding in a roundabout, while the roundabout speed and exits rule sets speeds, passing and signaling to exit. Remember: Slow, no passing, signal out.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Roundabout speeds are usually posted at fifteen to twenty-five miles per hour, you may not pass inside a multi-lane roundabout, and you signal right to exit.

question.text: Why are roundabouts used?

answer.text: Roundabouts are used to slow traffic, cut crashes and discourage commuters from cutting through neighborhoods.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "To raise speeds", but they slow traffic. Remember: Roundabouts calm traffic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Roundabouts are used to slow traffic, cut crashes and discourage commuters from cutting through neighborhoods.

question.text: Which side of the splitter island do you keep to, and may you stop inside a roundabout?

answer.text: Keep to the right of the splitter island when approaching a roundabout, and once inside do not stop unless a sign, signal or officer tells you to.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Yes, whenever you like", but only when directed. Remember: Right of the island.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Keep to the right of the splitter island when approaching a roundabout, and once inside do not stop unless a sign, signal or officer tells you to.

question.text: What should you watch for in a multi-lane roundabout?

answer.text: In a multi-lane roundabout be ready to yield to vehicles crossing in front of you from the inside lane to exit, and go around again if you miss your street.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Stop and back up", but go around again. Remember: Yield to exiting cars.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a multi-lane roundabout be ready to yield to vehicles crossing in front of you from the inside lane to exit, and go around again if you miss your street.

question.text: Where may you not make a U-turn?

answer.text: You may not make a U-turn at an intersection controlled by a signal or officer, or anywhere you cannot see five hundred feet of traffic both ways.

teaching.text: the u-turn bans rule bans U-turns at controlled intersections and without five hundred feet of view, while the more u-turn bans rule adds city mid-block and posted bans. Remember: No U-turn at signals.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may not make a U-turn at an intersection controlled by a signal or officer, or anywhere you cannot see five hundred feet of traffic both ways.

question.text: Where else are U-turns banned?

answer.text: U-turns are also banned between intersections in a city and wherever signs or markings forbid them; driving around the block is safer.

teaching.text: the u-turn bans rule bans U-turns at controlled intersections and without five hundred feet of view, while the more u-turn bans rule adds city mid-block and posted bans. Remember: Go around the block.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: U-turns are also banned between intersections in a city and wherever signs or markings forbid them; driving around the block is safer.

question.text: Can towns ban U-turns entirely?

answer.text: Some towns and cities ban U-turns on their streets entirely, so check with local police.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Assume they are always legal", but some towns ban them; check with police. Remember: Local bans exist.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Some towns and cities ban U-turns on their streets entirely, so check with local police.

question.text: Are U-turns legal on interstates, and who may use median crossovers?

answer.text: U-turns on interstates are illegal, and median emergency crossovers are only for emergency and maintenance vehicles.

teaching.text: the no interstate u-turns rule bans interstate U-turns, and the where crossovers exist rule says crossovers exist only on four-lane highways, not for regular interstate traffic. Remember: No interstate U-turns.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: U-turns on interstates are illegal, and median emergency crossovers are only for emergency and maintenance vehicles.

question.text: What should you do if you miss an interstate exit?

answer.text: If you miss an interstate exit or are stuck in a jam, drive on to the next exit; cutting across the median is illegal.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Cross the median", but that is illegal. Remember: Take the next exit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you miss an interstate exit or are stuck in a jam, drive on to the next exit; cutting across the median is illegal.

question.text: How much of a road with no center line should you give oncoming drivers?

answer.text: On a road with no center line, give oncoming drivers at least half of the road.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "A quarter of the road", but give at least half. Remember: Give half.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a road with no center line, give oncoming drivers at least half of the road.

question.text: What does a yellow line on your right mean?

answer.text: White on your right, yellow on your left: if the yellow line is on your right, you are on the wrong side and must pull over at once.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Keep going, it is normal", but you are on the wrong side. Remember: Yellow right means wrong.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: White on your right, yellow on your left: if the yellow line is on your right, you are on the wrong side and must pull over at once.

question.text: When may you drive left of center?

answer.text: Drive left of center only to pass, to get around an obstruction, on a one-way road or to turn left, and go around crashes to the right when possible.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Whenever it is faster", but only in the listed cases. Remember: Left of center rarely.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drive left of center only to pass, to get around an obstruction, on a one-way road or to turn left, and go around crashes to the right when possible.

question.text: What is the center lane of a three- or five-lane road for?

answer.text: The center lane of a two-way road with three or five lanes is used only for left turns.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Passing", but it is only for left turns. Remember: Center lane for left turns.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The center lane of a two-way road with three or five lanes is used only for left turns.

question.text: Which side of a divided highway must you use, and where may you cross?

answer.text: On a divided highway always use the road on the right, and cross the median only at an authorized crossover or intersection or when directed.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Anywhere it looks flat", but only at authorized crossings. Remember: Stay right of the median.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a divided highway always use the road on the right, and cross the median only at an authorized crossover or intersection or when directed.

question.text: What do red reflectors facing you on the lane lines mean?

answer.text: Red reflectors facing you on the lane lines mean you are driving the wrong way and could hit someone head on.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "A lane is ending", but they mean you are going the wrong way. Remember: Red reflectors, wrong way.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Red reflectors facing you on the lane lines mean you are driving the wrong way and could hit someone head on.

question.text: How do two-lane and four-lane highway center markings differ?

answer.text: A two-lane highway has a single broken yellow center line, while a four-lane highway has two solid yellow lines in the middle and dashed white lines between same-direction lanes.

teaching.text: the center line colors rule gives center line colors by street type, while the two-lane versus four-lane markings rule contrasts two-lane and four-lane highway center markings. Remember: Broken versus double solid.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A two-lane highway has a single broken yellow center line, while a four-lane highway has two solid yellow lines in the middle and dashed white lines between same-direction lanes.

question.text: Where do median crossovers exist?

answer.text: Median crossovers exist only at paved openings on four-lane highways; interstates have none for regular traffic.

teaching.text: the no interstate u-turns rule bans interstate U-turns, and the where crossovers exist rule says crossovers exist only on four-lane highways, not for regular interstate traffic. Remember: Crossovers on four-lanes only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Median crossovers exist only at paved openings on four-lane highways; interstates have none for regular traffic.

question.text: What should you do if a car is already waiting in a highway crossover?

answer.text: When a car is already waiting in a highway crossover, stay stopped in the left lane with your signal on rather than pulling in behind it, which could cause a head-on crash.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Pull in behind it", but that could cause a head-on crash. Remember: Wait in the left lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a car is already waiting in a highway crossover, stay stopped in the left lane with your signal on rather than pulling in behind it, which could cause a head-on crash.

question.text: What does a lane with both turn and straight arrows allow?

answer.text: A lane with both a turn arrow and a straight arrow lets you go either way, following normal right-of-way rules unless a protected arrow is showing.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Turning only", but it allows either. Remember: Either way allowed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A lane with both a turn arrow and a straight arrow lets you go either way, following normal right-of-way rules unless a protected arrow is showing.

question.text: What is a shared center turn lane for, and how far may you drive in it?

answer.text: A shared center turn lane is only for left turns from either direction, may not be used for passing, and may not be driven in for more than three hundred feet.

teaching.text: the shared center turn lane rule limits the shared center turn lane to left turns, and the first into the center lane rule gives the right-of-way to the first driver in. Remember: Left turns, short distance.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A shared center turn lane is only for left turns from either direction, may not be used for passing, and may not be driven in for more than three hundred feet.

question.text: Who has the right-of-way when two drivers enter a shared center turn lane?

answer.text: When drivers from opposite directions enter a shared center turn lane, the first one in has the right-of-way.

teaching.text: the shared center turn lane rule limits the shared center turn lane to left turns, and the first into the center lane rule gives the right-of-way to the first driver in. Remember: First in goes first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When drivers from opposite directions enter a shared center turn lane, the first one in has the right-of-way.

question.text: How should you use a shared center turn lane?

answer.text: Enter a shared center turn lane just before your turn, never ride in it to reach a turn lane at the next intersection, and you may use it to wait before merging right from a side street.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Several blocks early", but enter just before your turn. Remember: Enter just before turning.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Enter a shared center turn lane just before your turn, never ride in it to reach a turn lane at the next intersection, and you may use it to wait before merging right from a side street.

question.text: What do the signals over reversible lanes mean?

answer.text: Over reversible lanes, a green arrow means you may use the lane, a red X means you may not, a flashing yellow X means turns only, and a steady yellow X means leave the lane soon.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Turns only", but that is a flashing yellow X. Remember: Arrow go, X no.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Over reversible lanes, a green arrow means you may use the lane, a red X means you may not, a flashing yellow X means turns only, and a steady yellow X means leave the lane soon.

question.text: Who may use a reserved lane marked with a white diamond?

answer.text: Reserved lanes marked by a white diamond are for buses, bicycles or HOV car pools only, though you may cross one to turn within the next half block.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "No, never", but you may cross it to turn within the next half block. Remember: Diamond lanes reserved.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Reserved lanes marked by a white diamond are for buses, bicycles or HOV car pools only, though you may cross one to turn within the next half block.

question.text: What does an HOV two sign mean?

answer.text: An HOV two sign means at least two people must be in the vehicle to use that lane, and signs give the days and hours the limit applies.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Two lanes are open", but it means at least two people. Remember: Two people minimum.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An HOV two sign means at least two people must be in the vehicle to use that lane, and signs give the days and hours the limit applies.

question.text: What steps should you take to change lanes?

answer.text: To change lanes, check your mirrors, signal, look over your shoulder toward your move, check blind spots, and then move over gradually.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Turning off your signal", but signal before and during the move. Remember: Mirror, signal, shoulder, move.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To change lanes, check your mirrors, signal, look over your shoulder toward your move, check blind spots, and then move over gradually.

question.text: What should you do when the driver ahead signals a lane change?

answer.text: When the driver ahead signals a lane change, slow and leave room, and do not speed up or change lanes until they have finished.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Speed up to block", but slow and leave room. Remember: Make room.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When the driver ahead signals a lane change, slow and leave room, and do not speed up or change lanes until they have finished.

question.text: Before passing, how should you judge an oncoming vehicle you can see?

answer.text: Before passing, assume that any oncoming vehicle you can see is too close, and when in doubt stay in your lane.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Assume it is far enough away", but assume it is too close. Remember: Assume it is too close.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before passing, assume that any oncoming vehicle you can see is too close, and when in doubt stay in your lane.

question.text: Why are passing crashes so dangerous?

answer.text: Passing crashes are often fatal: cutting back too soon risks a sideswipe, and cutting back too late risks a head-on collision.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "A head-on collision", but that comes from cutting back too late. Remember: Too soon or too late.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing crashes are often fatal: cutting back too soon risks a sideswipe, and cutting back too late risks a head-on collision.

question.text: What does needing to swing over to look ahead before passing tell you?

answer.text: Do not swing across the center line to look ahead before passing; needing to do so means you are following too closely or lack the sight distance to pass.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "It is a safe passing method", but it means you should not pass. Remember: Too close to pass.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not swing across the center line to look ahead before passing; needing to do so means you are following too closely or lack the sight distance to pass.

question.text: Why avoid passing at night on unfamiliar roads?

answer.text: Avoid passing at night on unfamiliar roads, because it is harder to see where the passing zone ends.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Headlights are dimmer", but the reason is seeing where the zone ends. Remember: Zones hard to see at night.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Avoid passing at night on unfamiliar roads, because it is harder to see where the passing zone ends.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Zones hard to see at night

question.text: When may you return to your lane after passing?

answer.text: Return to your lane after passing only when you can see the whole passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, and then cancel your signal.

teaching.text: the returning after a pass rule says return only when the whole passed car shows in your mirror, while the passing several vehicles rule covers passing several vehicles at once. Remember: Whole car in the mirror.

question.text: Is passing several vehicles at once legal and safe?

answer.text: Passing several vehicles at once is not illegal in Tennessee but is generally unsafe, and should only be tried if you can be back in your lane one hundred feet before a no-passing marking or oncoming car.

teaching.text: the returning after a pass rule says return only when the whole passed car shows in your mirror, while the passing several vehicles rule covers passing several vehicles at once. Remember: Legal but risky.

question.text: When may you pass on the right?

answer.text: You may pass on the right only when the car ahead is turning left or the road has room for two or more moving lanes your way, and never by leaving the pavement.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Whenever the shoulder is wide", but never by leaving the pavement. Remember: Right pass rarely, never off-road.

question.text: Where must you never pass on the right?

answer.text: Never pass on the right in a bike lane, a parking lane, or an emergency lane within sight of a signal or stop sign; the driver passing on the right is at fault if the car ahead turns right.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "The driver turning right", but the driver passing on the right is at fault. Remember: Never bike or parking lanes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never pass on the right in a bike lane, a parking lane, or an emergency lane within sight of a signal or stop sign; the driver passing on the right is at fault if the car ahead turns right.

question.text: Where should you not pass?

answer.text: Do not pass near an intersection, railroad crossing, narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel, or when approaching a hill or curve.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "On a straight, clear road with a broken line", but that can be a safe place to pass. Remember: No passing near hazards.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not pass near an intersection, railroad crossing, narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel, or when approaching a hill or curve.

question.text: Why should you never pass a car stopped for pedestrians?

answer.text: Never pass a car that has stopped for pedestrians in a crosswalk, a frequent cause of pedestrian deaths.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never pass a car that has stopped for pedestrians in a crosswalk, a frequent cause of pedestrian deaths.

question.text: When else is passing forbidden?

answer.text: Do not pass when the solid yellow line is on your side or when a school or church bus has its lights flashing and stop arm out.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Yes, slowly", but do not pass. Remember: Solid on your side, no.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not pass when the solid yellow line is on your side or when a school or church bus has its lights flashing and stop arm out.

question.text: How far before a crosswalk should you stop on a multi-lane road?

answer.text: On a multi-lane road, stop about thirty feet before a crosswalk so you do not hide crossing pedestrians from drivers in other lanes.

teaching.text: the car stopped for pedestrians rule bans passing a car stopped for pedestrians, and the stop back from a crosswalk rule says stop well back of a crosswalk on multi-lane roads. Remember: Stop thirty feet back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a multi-lane road, stop about thirty feet before a crosswalk so you do not hide crossing pedestrians from drivers in other lanes.

question.text: What does the end of a no-passing zone mean?

answer.text: The end of a no-passing zone only means you can see farther; you still must judge whether passing is safe.

question.text: May you cross a solid yellow line to turn left in a no-passing zone?

answer.text: In a no-passing zone you may still cross the solid yellow line to turn left into or out of an alley, intersection, private road or driveway.

teaching.text: the turning across a no-passing line rule lets you cross a solid line to turn into a driveway in a no-passing zone, while the end of a no-passing zone rule says the zone's end only means you can see farther. Remember: Turning across is allowed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a no-passing zone you may still cross the solid yellow line to turn left into or out of an alley, intersection, private road or driveway.

question.text: What passing moves are banned on shoulders and between lanes?

answer.text: Do not pass on the right shoulder, and do not weave from lane to lane to get ahead of traffic.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Staying in one lane", but that is fine. Remember: No shoulder, no weaving.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not pass on the right shoulder, and do not weave from lane to lane to get ahead of traffic.

question.text: What should you do while someone passes you?

answer.text: When someone is passing you, stay in your lane, keep to the right and hold your speed, never speeding up to block them.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Speed up", but never speed up to block them. Remember: Hold lane, hold speed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When someone is passing you, stay in your lane, keep to the right and hold your speed, never speeding up to block them.

question.text: What should you do if an oncoming car appears while you are being passed?

answer.text: If an oncoming car appears while you are being passed, slow down so the passing driver can pull back in ahead of you.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Speed up", but slow down. Remember: Slow to let them in.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If an oncoming car appears while you are being passed, slow down so the passing driver can pull back in ahead of you.

question.text: How much space does Tennessee law require when passing a bicycle?

answer.text: Tennessee law requires at least three feet of space when passing a bicycle going your way, kept until you are safely past.

teaching.text: the three feet for bicycles rule requires three feet when passing a bicycle, and the passing bicyclists safely rule bans passing between a bicyclist and oncoming traffic on a two-lane road. Remember: Three feet for bikes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Tennessee law requires at least three feet of space when passing a bicycle going your way, kept until you are safely past.

question.text: How should you pass a bicyclist on a two-lane road?

answer.text: Never pass between a bicyclist and oncoming traffic on a two-lane road, and do not pass where it would squeeze the rider toward parked cars.

teaching.text: the three feet for bicycles rule requires three feet when passing a bicycle, and the passing bicyclists safely rule bans passing between a bicyclist and oncoming traffic on a two-lane road. Remember: Never squeeze a cyclist.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never pass between a bicyclist and oncoming traffic on a two-lane road, and do not pass where it would squeeze the rider toward parked cars.

question.text: What does it mean if you cannot see a truck's side mirrors?

answer.text: If you cannot see a truck's side mirrors, its driver cannot see you, and lingering beside a truck keeps you in its blind spot.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "The truck has no mirrors", but it means the driver cannot see you. Remember: No mirrors, no view.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you cannot see a truck's side mirrors, its driver cannot see you, and lingering beside a truck keeps you in its blind spot.

question.text: Why should you never pull in front of a truck and slow down?

answer.text: Never pull in front of a truck or bus and slow down, because it removes the truck driver's safety cushion.

teaching.text: the do not cut in front of trucks rule says never cut in and slow in front of a truck, while the passing trucks on grades rule explains passing trucks on level ground, upgrades and downgrades. Remember: Keep the truck's cushion.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never pull in front of a truck or bus and slow down, because it removes the truck driver's safety cushion.

question.text: How does passing a truck change on level ground, upgrades and downgrades?

answer.text: Passing a truck takes longer on level ground, is easier on an upgrade where it slows, and may need more speed on a downgrade, but you still may not exceed the limit.

teaching.text: the do not cut in front of trucks rule says never cut in and slow in front of a truck, while the passing trucks on grades rule explains passing trucks on level ground, upgrades and downgrades. Remember: Grades change the pass.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing a truck takes longer on level ground, is easier on an upgrade where it slows, and may need more speed on a downgrade, but you still may not exceed the limit.

question.text: When may you back into a travel lane?

answer.text: Never back into a travel lane except into a parallel parking space, and remember that backing is the maneuver new drivers most often fail on the road test.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Whenever traffic is light", but only into a parallel parking space. Remember: Back only into parking.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never back into a travel lane except into a parallel parking space, and remember that backing is the maneuver new drivers most often fail on the road test.

question.text: How should you prepare to back up?

answer.text: Before backing, check behind the vehicle before getting in, then look through the rear window instead of relying only on mirrors or leaning out the door.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Rely only on the mirrors", but look through the rear window. Remember: Look behind, then back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before backing, check behind the vehicle before getting in, then look through the rear window instead of relying only on mirrors or leaning out the door.

question.text: Where is backing illegal?

answer.text: Backing from a driveway into an intersection is illegal, and so is backing up on an interstate.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Backing into a parallel space", but that is allowed. Remember: No backing on interstates.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Backing from a driveway into an intersection is illegal, and so is backing up on an interstate.

question.text: When may you stop in a travel lane?

answer.text: Do not stop in a travel lane for any reason, such as being lost, a breakdown or dropping off a passenger; keep going until you can pull off.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Yes, with flashers", but keep going until you can pull off. Remember: Never stop in a lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not stop in a travel lane for any reason, such as being lost, a breakdown or dropping off a passenger; keep going until you can pull off.

question.text: What happens to the front of the car when backing out of an angle space?

answer.text: When backing out of an angle space, the front of the car swings opposite to the turn; stop and look again once you can see past the cars beside you.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "The same way as the turn", but it swings opposite. Remember: Front swings opposite.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When backing out of an angle space, the front of the car swings opposite to the turn; stop and look again once you can see past the cars beside you.

question.text: How should you park outside city limits?

answer.text: Outside city limits, park with all four wheels off the pavement if possible, leave at least eighteen feet of road for traffic, and be visible for two hundred feet both ways.

teaching.text: the wheel position on hills rule sets wheel position on hills, while the parking outside city limits rule sets how to park outside city limits. Remember: Wheels off, room for traffic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Outside city limits, park with all four wheels off the pavement if possible, leave at least eighteen feet of road for traffic, and be visible for two hundred feet both ways.

question.text: What should you do every time you park?

answer.text: Set the parking brake every time you park, leaving a manual car in gear or an automatic in park, especially on hills or near schools and playgrounds.

teaching.text: the set the parking brake rule says set the parking brake every time, while the no unattended running engine rule bans leaving the engine running in an unattended car. Remember: Set the brake.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Set the parking brake every time you park, leaving a manual car in gear or an automatic in park, especially on hills or near schools and playgrounds.

question.text: Is it legal to leave the engine running in an unattended car?

answer.text: Leaving the engine running in an unattended parked car is illegal; take the keys and lock the doors.

teaching.text: the set the parking brake rule says set the parking brake every time, while the no unattended running engine rule bans leaving the engine running in an unattended car. Remember: Keys out, doors locked.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Leaving the engine running in an unattended parked car is illegal; take the keys and lock the doors.

question.text: What must you do when pulling out of any parking space?

answer.text: Look, signal and yield whenever you pull out of any parking space, including a parallel space.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Pull out quickly", but look, signal and yield. Remember: Look, signal, yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Look, signal and yield whenever you pull out of any parking space, including a parallel space.

question.text: Which way should your front wheels point when parking on a hill?

answer.text: On a downhill with a curb, or on any hill without a curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road; uphill with a curb, turn them away from the curb.

teaching.text: the wheel position on hills rule sets wheel position on hills, while the parking outside city limits rule sets how to park outside city limits. Remember: Down to the curb, up away.

question.text: What are the minimum parking distances from hydrants, crosswalks, signals and railroad crossings?

answer.text: Parking is illegal within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant, within twenty feet of a crosswalk, within thirty feet of a traffic signal or stop sign, and within fifty feet of a railroad crossing.

teaching.text: the no-parking distances rule sets parking distances from hydrants, crosswalks, signals and railroad crossings, while the fire station parking distances rule sets the distances from a fire station driveway. Remember: Fifteen, twenty, thirty, fifty.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parking is illegal within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant, within twenty feet of a crosswalk, within thirty feet of a traffic signal or stop sign, and within fifty feet of a railroad crossing.

question.text: Is double parking legal, and when may you use four-way flashers?

answer.text: Double parking is illegal, and four-way flashers may be used after dark when a vehicle is disabled or creates a hazard.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "To double park", but double parking is illegal. Remember: No double parking.

question.text: Name other places where parking is illegal.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parking is also illegal in front of a driveway, in an intersection or fire lane, on a sidewalk, bridge or tunnel, on interstate ramps unless disabled, and on an interstate shoulder except in an emergency.

question.text: How far from a fire station driveway must you park?

answer.text: Keep at least twenty feet from a fire station driveway when parking on its side of the street, and at least seventy-five feet when parking across from it.

teaching.text: the no-parking distances rule sets parking distances from hydrants, crosswalks, signals and railroad crossings, while the fire station parking distances rule sets the distances from a fire station driveway. Remember: Twenty same side, seventy-five across.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Keep at least twenty feet from a fire station driveway when parking on its side of the street, and at least seventy-five feet when parking across from it.

question.text: What rules can painted curbs set?

answer.text: Painted curbs set special rules: some allow stopping only to pick up or drop off passengers, some only to load or unload with the driver staying, and some forbid stopping at all.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Mark a speed limit", but painted curbs set stopping rules. Remember: Curb paint sets limits.

question.text: How do you start a parallel park?

answer.text: To start parallel parking, stop beside the car ahead of the space, bumpers even, no closer than two feet, then back slowly with the wheel turned sharply right to about a forty-five-degree angle.

teaching.text: the starting a parallel park rule covers starting a parallel park, while the finishing a parallel park rule covers the finished distance from the curb. Remember: Even bumpers, back at angle.

question.text: How close to the curb should a finished parallel park be?

answer.text: A finished parallel park should leave you no more than eighteen inches from the curb, and check traffic before opening the driver's door.

teaching.text: the starting a parallel park rule covers starting a parallel park, while the finishing a parallel park rule covers the finished distance from the curb. Remember: Within eighteen inches.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A finished parallel park should leave you no more than eighteen inches from the curb, and check traffic before opening the driver's door.

question.text: What should you do if your car breaks down and cannot leave the road?

answer.text: If your car breaks down and cannot leave the road, raise the hood or tie a cloth to the left door handle or antenna, turn on the flashers and lock up.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If your car breaks down and cannot leave the road, raise the hood or tie a cloth to the left door handle or antenna, turn on the flashers and lock up.

question.text: Is walking on an interstate legal?

answer.text: Walking on an interstate is illegal, so except in an extreme emergency stay in a disabled car until an officer or helper arrives.

teaching.text: A tempting wrong answer is "Walk to the next exit", but walking on an interstate is illegal. Remember: Stay with the car.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Walking on an interstate is illegal, so except in an extreme emergency stay in a disabled car until an officer or helper arrives.

question.text: Who may park in a handicap space, and what is the penalty for misuse?

answer.text: Handicap spaces are only for a vehicle with a valid placard or plate that is carrying its holder; anyone else parking there commits a misdemeanor with a one hundred dollars fine and may be towed.
